children: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, fell by 1.4% to 3,575 points on Monday, snapping a three-day advance but staying near its highest levels since October 2021.

The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, slumped by 2.2% to 6,286 points, also breaking a three-day wining streak but remaining close to its peak since December 2023.
At the same time, the panamax index, which tracks vessels carrying around 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, was down for a second session, falling 0.7% tp 2,431 points.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index went up by 0.4% to 1,682 points.

title: Baltic Dry Index Breaks 3-Day Advance
